name: Bioelectric Induction Lance BIL-3 'Lamprey'
description:
The BIL-3 is a 90-centimeter rigid lance constructed around a core of layered piezoelectric crystal stacks and a helical induction coil running its full length. When the lance tip contacts a target — biological or electronic — it activates a continuous induction cycle that draws bioelectric current from living tissue or residual charge from electronic systems, feeding it back through the coil into an internal capacitor bank. The effect on biological targets is a sustained drain sensation described by survivors as 'being pulled from the inside,' accompanied by progressive muscular depolarization that renders limbs unresponsive within 3-5 seconds of sustained contact.

What makes the BIL-3 genuinely unusual among melee weapons is its dual function as a charging platform. The harvested energy is stored in the onboard capacitor and can be discharged back through the lance tip as a focused galvanic burst — essentially using the target's own bioelectric signature as ammunition. Operators who maintain contact long enough to achieve a full capacitor cycle can release the stored charge in a single pulse that mimics the target's own neural frequency pattern, causing a particularly disorienting feedback effect in biological targets and a signature-matched surge in electronic systems that bypasses standard surge protection.

HELIX BIOSYSTEMS developed the BIL-3 ostensibly as a 'bioelectric diagnostic probe' for field medical applications, a designation that strains credulity given its lance form factor and combat-optimized grip. The medical cover has nonetheless kept it in a regulatory gray zone — it is technically licensed as a medical instrument, which means it can be transported and owned without a weapons permit, a loophole that has made it popular among operators who need to pass legal checkpoints without triggering weapons flags.
legality: Licensed (classified as medical instrument — exploited loophole)
specifications:
length: 90 cm
weight: 1.4 kg
core material: Layered PZT crystal stack over carbon-fiber spine
induction range: Contact — effective to 2mm gap with conductive medium
capacitor capacity: 800 mAh, reaches full charge after 6 seconds sustained contact
discharge mode: Manual trigger — full capacitor dump in 0.3 seconds
biological effect onset: Muscular depolarization in 3-5 seconds sustained contact
electronic effect: Signature-matched surge — bypasses standard surge protection rated below Grade 4
regulatory classification: Class II Bioelectric Diagnostic Instrument (HELIX filing #BB-2291)
tactical_use: Experienced operators use the BIL-3 in a two-phase approach: initial contact to begin the drain cycle and trigger muscular depolarization, followed by a controlled hold while the capacitor charges, then a decisive discharge pulse once the target's mobility is compromised. Against electronic targets — drones, security panels, augmentation control units — the signature-matched discharge is particularly effective for destroying systems without leaving the broad electromagnetic trace of a conventional EMP. Some operators carry the BIL-3 specifically for anti-augmentation work, targeting the neural interface clusters at the base of the skull where bioelectric activity is densest.
cultural_context: The BIL-3's medical classification has made it the weapon of choice for a specific archetype in GLMZ: the professional who needs to move through legitimate spaces. Corporate fixers, licensed augmentation technicians moonlighting as enforcers, and well-connected street operators who have the paperwork to back up their 'diagnostic equipment' all favor it. There is an open secret in certain circles that HELIX BIOSYSTEMS knows exactly what its 'diagnostic probe' is being used for and has quietly lobbied to maintain the regulatory classification, as the gray-market demand has made the BIL-3 their most profitable single product line.
known_users: Corporate fixers and mid-level enforcers requiring legal checkpoint clearance
Augmentation black-market technicians with dual-use tool kits
HELIX BIOSYSTEMS field representatives (officially for demonstration purposes)
Anti-augmentation extremist cells (ironic given the manufacturer)
Bounty hunters operating in jurisdictions with strict weapons licensing
story_hooks: A HELIX BIOSYSTEMS lobbyist is murdered with a BIL-3, and the discharge signature logged by the victim's augmentation system matches the lobbyist's own bioelectric profile — suggesting the weapon was charged on the victim before being turned against them, or that someone is very good at spoofing signatures.

The regulatory classification loophole is about to be closed by a new GLMZ municipal ordinance, and someone is paying very well to ensure that ordinance doesn't pass — the players are hired either to protect the vote or to find out who's funding the opposition.

A player character's augmentation begins malfunctioning in a pattern consistent with repeated low-level bioelectric drain — someone has been using a BIL-3 on them during their sleep cycles, harvesting charge without triggering the weapon's disabling threshold.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, organic-looking lance with a tapered profile that suggests biological rather than mechanical engineering. The shaft has a subtle helical twist visible along its length, and the tip comes to a precise, almost surgical point. The overall impression is of a medical instrument that happens to be lethally sharp—clinical and purposeful rather than brutish.
physical_description.dimensions: 90 cm total length; 2.2 cm shaft diameter at grip, tapering to 0.8 cm at tip; grip section 15 cm
physical_description.weight_description: Deceptively light—1.4 kg distributed evenly along the shaft creates excellent balance. Feels almost weightless in motion but carries substantial presence due to its rigidity and the subtle vibration of the induction coil when powered.
physical_description.primary_material: Carbon-fiber spine wrapped in layered PZT piezoelectric crystal stacks; visible translucent crystalline layers along the shaft with a semi-flexible polymer sheath binding them
physical_description.finish: Matte charcoal with an iridescent blue-violet sheen across the crystal layers that shifts in light; the tip is polished to a mirror finish for conductivity
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal gray body with deep iridescent blue-purple crystal layers; grip section in black synthetic with silver accent trim; subtle bioluminescent cyan capacitor indicator running along the shaft's spine
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured black synthetic polymer with microscopic conductive threading woven through; slightly tacky, designed for secure contact even with sweat or augmentation fluid; subtle ridges provide feedback during the drain cycle
distinctive_features: Helical twist pattern visible along crystal layers—not decorative, but the physical manifestation of the induction coil spiral
Bioluminescent charge indicator strip running 8 cm up from the grip, glowing cyan when capacitor is charging, shifting to amber at 75% charge, bright white when fully charged
Microscopic etched grid pattern around the tip—conductivity enhancement matrix
Three small sensor ports (1 cm diameter) spaced along the upper shaft—diagnostic readouts for HELIX service technicians, repurposed for visual feedback by operators
Faint residual corona effect visible around the tip when charged—barely perceptible shimmer in dark conditions
Wear patterns around the tip and lower shaft from sustained contact with targets—micro-scarring in the polymer sheath
Grip section has a subtle swell at the pommel end (3 cm sphere) for counterbalance and to house part of the capacitor bank
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: HELIX BIOSYSTEMS logo (stylized double helix) etched into the pommel in silver; regulatory classification plate (15 mm × 8 mm) adhesive-mounted 5 cm below the grip reading 'CLASS II BIOELECTRIC DIAGNOSTIC INSTRUMENT BB-2291'; small serial number laser-burned into the shaft 20 cm from the tip
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained examples show minimal wear; heavy-use variants display micro-fractures in the outer polymer sheath (easily repairable), scuffing around the tip from repeated contact, and faint burn marks where the capacitor has discharged. The indicator strip may be dimmed or flickering in neglected units. Black market variants sometimes have removed or defaced HELIX markings.
